Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of current findings: Acute diarrheal illness lasting 3 days with loose, watery stools 6–7 times/day; left lower quadrant crampy abdominal pain; intermittent feverish sensation; initial vomiting (now resolved); decreased appetite; able to maintain fluids; no blood in stool; no nocturnal symptoms reported. Recent takeout meal (Chinese restaurant) ~4 days prior. Known asthma, well-controlled on inhaler. Work and daily activities affected due to frequent toilet visits.
- Diagnostic impression consistent with differential diagnoses in DDx:
  - Viral gastroenteritis (High likelihood): Acute onset after possible exposure; watery diarrhea without blood; initial vomiting and feverish sensation align with a viral infectious gastroenteritis. No alternate red flags documented.
  - Bacterial gastroenteritis/food poisoning (Moderate likelihood): Takeout exposure 4 days before symptoms; diarrhea and cramps possible with bacterial etiologies; absence of blood does not exclude bacteria.
  - Post-infectious lactose intolerance / IBD flare (Low likelihood): Left-sided cramps and diarrhea after GI illness considered; no prior IBD history or chronic pattern documented.
  - Giardia or other parasitic enteritis (Low likelihood): Diarrhea present; timeline more typical for non-parasitic etiologies.
- Conflicts: Not recorded
- Plan to monitor and manage conservatively; stool testing considered if symptoms persist or worsen

Management Plan
- Main plan: Conservative management with emphasis on hydration and symptomatic care
  - Oral rehydration: Use Dioralyte or similar electrolyte solution to replenish fluids and minerals
  - Hydration and diet: Maintain fluid intake; light foods (soups, smoothies, liquid/soft foods) as tolerated
  - Antipyretic/analgesic: Paracetamol as needed for fever/weakness (two tablets up to four times daily); note: dose/route/frequency not documented
  - Activity/work: Advise taking 2–3 days off work to rest while infection resolves
  - Follow-up: Reassess if no improvement within 3–4 days; may consider stool testing if symptoms persist
  - Antibiotics: Not indicated at this time
- Consider pathology or additional testing: Stool sample for testing if symptoms persist or recur
